title: The emitted store builds a verified TLS configuration
when: Builds a database configuration with sslmode verify-full.
then: Expects a TLS configuration that verifies the server and requires TLS 1.2 or later.

title: The emitted store refuses each weak sslmode
when: Builds a database configuration for each weak sslmode while the test exception setting is 0.
then: Expects each weak mode refused.

title: The emitted store keeps the loopback exception narrow
when: Builds a database configuration for each host while the test exception setting is 1, and then for each other value of the setting.
then: Expects plaintext allowed only to a literal loopback address, an unverified TLS fallback refused, and a safe error for any other value of the setting.

title: The emitted store checks the chain, the server name and the TLS version on a real connection
when: Opens a real TLS connection with a valid certificate, then with a wrong server name, then with a wrong trust root.
then: Expects the valid certificate accepted and both failures refused.

title: The cursor value is bound and related access holds
when: Reads under a related access filter, then with an injection string as the cursor, then after deleting one related row with CursorAll.
then: Expects only the two permitted rows, no hidden row for the injection cursor, and the deleted related row granting no access.
notes: Proved by TestCursorBindsInputAndKeepsRelatedAccess; its name or a subtest must carry this ID. Partial: the cursor test shows the access filter is kept on list reads; no test yet covers single reads and writes.

title: A target value is a bound parameter
when: Creates and deletes a Placement whose target holds quotes, a placeholder, a non-ASCII character, a backslash and brackets, observes with an empty, oversized, invalid UTF-8 and NUL target, then with the real one.
then: Expects the four invalid targets refused and the opaque target completing its owner.
notes: Proved by TestOpaqueTargetValuesStayBoundParameters; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: An invalid key page request runs no query
when: On an uninitialized store, requests pages with a wrong-case entity, an empty and an oversized scope, a cursor with NUL, invalid UTF-8 and 257 bytes, limits of 0, 1001 and -1, a nil context, and a canceled context.
then: Expects ErrResourceState for every invalid request and the nil context, and Canceled for the canceled one, with no query possible.
notes: Proved by TestResourceStateKeysRejectInvalidInput; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The revision counts every write and ignores the caller
when: Creates a record with a caller revision of 800, updates through raw SQL with a forged revision, writes with the old observation, writes with the current revision and a forged value, replaces ordinarily, and migrates again.
then: Expects revision 1 at insert, 2 after raw SQL, ErrVersionConflict with no change for the old observation, 3 after the accepted conditional write, 4 after the replace, and 4 after the repeated migration.
notes: Proved by TestResourceVersionCoversAllWritesAndRejectsOldObservation; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Only one concurrent conditional writer succeeds
when: Runs two conditional writes against revision 1 at the same time.
then: Expects exactly one success, one ErrVersionConflict, and revision 2.
notes: Proved by TestOnlyOneConcurrentVersionWriterSucceeds; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A conflict rolls back the transaction's other work
when: Creates another record and then writes conditionally with a stale revision in one transaction.
then: Expects ErrVersionConflict, the other record absent, and the target revision unchanged.
notes: Proved by TestResourceVersionConflictRollsBackWork; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A cursor page follows the database order with one query
when: Under the C and the ICU collation, creates six mixed-case records with two deleted, then pages through CursorLive, CursorAll and CursorDeleted with a limit of 2, selected fields, an implicit filter and a text match, counting queries, and finally lists ordinarily.
then: Expects one SELECT and no count per page, at most two rows, the database's own order even where it differs from Go string order, exact More and NextID, the right visibility per mode, and the ordinary list keeping its count.
notes: Proved by TestCursorPagesUseDatabaseOrderWithoutCounts; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Every list predicate uses the current observation
when: With standard_conforming_strings off and a declared unobserved value holding a backslash, quote and placeholder, makes one stale and one current observation, then runs a scope, an implicit filter, a row filter, a text match, two related filters and a confirmed filter through List, ReadCursor and CountOnly, reads sparse lists, orders by the field, and deletes the stale row.
then: Expects the stored value kept in Get, every predicate and count matching the projected value, the cursor agreeing, sparse rows keeping their metadata, the order using the projection, and the deleted row absent.
notes: Proved by TestCurrentObservationsControlListsAndPredicates; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A cursor read shares the transaction and stops on cancellation
when: Reads a cursor on the transaction store after an uncommitted create, then reads under a 30 ms context while another session holds an exclusive table lock.
then: Expects the uncommitted row in the transaction's page, and the blocked read to fail within two seconds.
notes: Proved by TestCursorUsesTransactionAndHonorsCancellation; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A binding write outside or after a transaction is refused and a failure blocks commit
when: Calls BindEffect and CloseEffectBinding outside a transaction, ignores a conflicting second registration inside one, uses the retained scope after it closed, sends six invalid inputs, and registers under a canceled context.
then: Expects ErrTransactionRequired, ErrEffectBindingConflict with no row committed, ErrTransactionClosed for the retained scope, ErrEffectBinding for every invalid input, Canceled for the canceled call, and no row in the table.
notes: Proved by TestEffectBindingFailureRollsBackAndRequiresActiveTransaction; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A rejected notification blocks commit
when: For an invalid JSON payload, a duplicate ID, a 33rd message, an oversized payload and a missing queue schema, creates a record and ignores the rejected notification.
then: Expects the transaction to fail, no record committed, and no partial batch.
notes: Proved by TestNotificationFailureRollsBack; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A notification without the outbox peer blocks commit
when: Creates and ignores a notification inside a scope on a store generated without the outbox peer.
then: Expects ErrNotificationsUnavailable and no record committed.
notes: Proved by TestUnavailableNotificationsPreventCommit; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A cleanup observation and its event commit together
when: Observes an owner and notifies in one transaction while the outbox rejects inserts, then repeats after the constraint is removed.
then: Expects the first transaction to fail with no observation kept, and the second to commit the observation with one event.
notes: Proved by TestCleanupObservationAndEventsRollbackTogether; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Finalization refuses live, incomplete, stale and unsupported resources
when: Tries to finalize a live resource, a deleted but incomplete one and a stale revision, also through direct SQL; completes both owners; finalizes inside a failing transaction, then with its event; reopens an owner; runs SQL that clears or moves the finalization; finalizes an unsupported entity.
then: Expects ErrVersionConflict for the live, incomplete and stale cases, the direct SQL refused, no finalization from the observations alone, nothing kept by the failed transaction, one event with the committed finalization at a higher revision and the same generation, the late observation leaving the finalization time unchanged, both reversal statements refused, and the unsupported entity refused.
notes: Proved by TestDeletionFinalizationIsPermanentAndTransactional; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Pending deletions appear only under the deleting options and keep access
when: Creates live, pending, finalized, access-denied and access-revoked resources, rebuilds the store, lists with IncludeDeleting and OnlyDeleting under a related access filter page by page, reads CursorVisible and CursorDeleting cursors, and calls Get, Replace and WithLockedResource on the pending and finalized rows.
then: Expects a count of two and pages holding only the live and pending rows, one pending-only count, the cursors returning the same visible IDs, and ErrNotFound without a callback from the three live-only operations.
notes: Proved by TestDeletionFinalizationVisibilityKeepsAccessAndPages; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Identity and deletion cannot be reversed
when: Changes a row's ID through SQL, soft-deletes it, clears deleted_at and physically deletes it through SQL, and writes to it conditionally at its current revision.
then: Expects the ID change refused, revision 2 after deletion, both reversal statements refused, and ErrVersionConflict for the write.
notes: Proved by TestVersionedIdentityAndDeletionCannotBeReversed; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The ledger records the bootstrap and a restart applies nothing
when: Migrates a fresh schema-generation database, reads the ledger, and migrates again.
then: Expects ledger rows with 001_initial first, and the same row count after the restart.
notes: Proved by TestMigrationLedgerRecordsBootstrapAndRestart; its name or a subtest must carry this ID. Partial: no test yet shows the application role cannot alter the ledger.

title: A new registration is applied once and recorded
when: Migrates, registers a new migration, migrates twice, and applies the same version through ApplyMigration.
then: Expects the new version recorded once and the re-application refused.
notes: Proved by TestMigrationLedgerAppliesNewRegistrations; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Digest drift and a foreign row are refused
when: Tampers with an applied row's digest and migrates, then restores it, inserts a foreign version, and migrates.
then: Expects ErrMigrationLedger both times.
notes: Proved by TestMigrationLedgerRejectsGapsAndDrift; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The emitted pool applies its defaults and bounds
when: Opens a pool with 29 invalid values across the four settings, then reads the defaults, an open limit of 1, and the boundary values 0, 1s and 24h.
then: Expects no pool and the error 'invalid database pool setting: <name>' for every invalid value, the defaults 16, 4, 30m and 5m, an idle default of 1 under an open limit of 1, and every boundary value accepted.
notes: Proved by TestPoolSettingsRejectInvalidValues; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The emitted pool holds its open limit and honors a waiting caller
when: Opens a pool with an open limit of 2 and an idle limit of 1, holds two connections, asks for a third under a 50 ms deadline and then under a canceled context, releases one, pings, and releases the other.
then: Expects no third connection, DeadlineExceeded and Canceled for the two waits, one wait in the statistics, a ping after the release, no connection in use at the end, at most one idle, and a connection closed for the idle limit.
notes: Proved by TestPoolLimitWaitCancellationAndRelease; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The store refuses a missing or altered key index
when: Drops the primary key, drops the key index, recreates it in another column order, recreates it with a predicate, disables the guard, drops NOT NULL and the check constraint, and enables row security, each on a fresh database, then opens the store.
then: Expects the store to refuse to open after each change.
notes: Proved by TestResourceStateSchemaGuard; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The store refuses a disabled revision trigger
when: Disables the revision trigger, opens the store, migrates, and opens it again.
then: Expects the first open refused and the second accepted.
notes: Proved by TestVersionStartupRejectsDisabledTrigger; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A null condition object is refused by the trigger
when: Sets the condition column to JSON null through SQL, then drops the column and opens the store.
then: Expects the null refused and the store refusing to open without the column.
notes: Proved by TestConditionSchemaAndDataAreRequired; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The emitted backend sets a strict active session cookie
when: Completes a login, sends a write through the API prefix with extra browser headers, restarts the backend, then signs out.
then: Expects the login cookie Lax and the active cookie Strict, both Secure, HttpOnly and host-only, no token in the session response, only the server access token and four permitted headers at the API, and no upstream Set-Cookie.

title: The completion document keeps the strict session cookie
when: Completes a protected application callback, then replays the same callback.
then: Expects a Strict, Secure, HttpOnly, host-only cookie, no session ID, token, code or state in the body, and 400 with no document for the replay.

title: The emitted backend sets a lax login cookie
when: Completes a login, sends a write through the API prefix with extra browser headers, restarts the backend, then signs out.
then: Expects the login cookie Lax and the active cookie Strict, both Secure, HttpOnly and host-only, no token in the session response, only the server access token and four permitted headers at the API, and no upstream Set-Cookie.

title: The emitted store encrypts session records and binds them to the cookie hash
when: Creates a session with an access and a refresh token, then reads the stored row and opens the record with another cookie ID and with one changed byte.
then: Expects a 32-byte hash, no plaintext token and no raw cookie ID in the row, and refusal of both the foreign cookie ID and the changed ciphertext.

title: The emitted session response holds no tokens
when: Completes a login, sends a write through the API prefix with extra browser headers, restarts the backend, then signs out.
then: Expects the login cookie Lax and the active cookie Strict, both Secure, HttpOnly and host-only, no token in the session response, only the server access token and four permitted headers at the API, and no upstream Set-Cookie.

title: The emitted backend refuses a mutation without an exact origin or a CSRF token
when: Sends thirteen requests with a missing, wrong, repeated or same-site origin, a missing or repeated CSRF header, a browser bearer token, a duplicate cookie, a bad method and an oversize body.
then: Expects the stated status for each case, and expects that no denied request reached the API.

title: The emitted backend refuses browser bearer credentials
when: Sends thirteen requests with a missing, wrong, repeated or same-site origin, a missing or repeated CSRF header, a browser bearer token, a duplicate cookie, a bad method and an oversize body.
then: Expects the stated status for each case, and expects that no denied request reached the API.

title: A captured asset refuses a browser bearer token
when: Reads each captured path from two backends with a session and a browser bearer token, among the other captured asset reads.
then: Expects 400 for each read that carries the bearer token.
notes: Conditional: the test skips when its fixture carries no captured assets, so whether it runs depends on the fixture rather than on the environment. Another test in the same folder takes the opposite branch, so both fixture shapes exist. Whether the default fixture reaches this test is not settled; check it before this proof is relied on.

title: The local application proxy refuses a browser bearer token
when: Sends an authenticated application request with a browser bearer token, among the other denied requests.
then: Expects 400.

title: The emitted proxy sends only server-held credentials
when: Completes a login, sends a write through the API prefix with extra browser headers, restarts the backend, then signs out.
then: Expects the login cookie Lax and the active cookie Strict, both Secure, HttpOnly and host-only, no token in the session response, only the server access token and four permitted headers at the API, and no upstream Set-Cookie.

title: Two emitted backend instances share one token renewal
when: Expires the access token, holds the provider refresh request, then asks for the session from both backend instances.
then: Expects the second instance to wait, both requests to succeed, the new access token at the API, and exactly one refresh request.

title: A second backend renews an expired application session
when: Expires the access token, then sends an application request through a second backend instance.
then: Expects success, and expects the application to receive the renewed access token.

title: A waiter for an active renewal has a deadline and keeps its cookie
when: Claims a renewal, then asks for the session, then asks again with a cancelled context.
then: Expects 503 with Retry-After inside three seconds, a retained session cookie, a cancelled waiter that stops inside one second, and no use of the refresh token.

title: A lost or stale renewal requires a new login and is not retried
when: Drops the provider refresh response, and separately ages an existing refresh claim past its deadline, then sends two API requests.
then: Expects 401 for both requests and expects no second refresh request.

title: A renewal claim with a lost commit requires a new login
when: Expires the access token, then loses the commit of the renewal claim.
then: Expects a session error, no stored session, and no provider refresh request.

title: A completed renewal cannot restore a session that sign-out removed
when: Starts a renewal on one instance, holds the provider request, then signs out on the second instance and releases the renewal.
then: Expects the sign-out to succeed, the later API request to return 401, and both the old and the rotated token to be revoked.

title: A renewal that spans a key switch cannot restore a signed-out session
when: Reads one old record through four key rings, writes through two mixed writers, then signs out during a key switch.
then: Expects every listed key to decrypt, the first key to encrypt new records, a removed key to lose access, and a renewal after sign-out to fail.

title: An application sign-out on one backend ends the session on another
when: Signs out without a CSRF token, then with one, and reads through a second backend instance after each.
then: Expects the first sign-out refused with the session kept, and 401 on the second backend after the valid sign-out.

title: The sign-out confirmation page does not sign out
when: Opens the confirmation page, then posts the form with a missing, null, foreign or repeated Origin value and with four invalid bodies.
then: Expects the page to keep the session and revoke nothing, Referrer-Policy same-origin on that page and no-referrer elsewhere, 403 or 400 for each invalid form, and sign-out only after a valid form.

title: The sign-out confirmation page does not sign out under native browser navigation
when: Opens the confirmation page in a headless browser with a session cookie and presses its submit button, once with the generated referrer policy and once with a no-referrer control.
then: Expects the generated page to post a same-origin form that signs out and revokes the session, and the control form to be refused with the session kept.
notes: Gated: the test skips unless STEGO_REQUIRE_BROWSER_LOGOUT is 1, and then it runs only in CI with Chrome or Chromium. It gives no proof on a developer workstation.

title: The sign-out confirmation page keeps its same-origin referrer policy
when: Opens the confirmation page, then posts the form with a missing, null, foreign or repeated Origin value and with four invalid bodies.
then: Expects the page to keep the session and revoke nothing, Referrer-Policy same-origin on that page and no-referrer elsewhere, 403 or 400 for each invalid form, and sign-out only after a valid form.

title: The sign-out confirmation page lets a native form send its Origin
when: Opens the confirmation page in a headless browser with a session cookie and presses its submit button, once with the generated referrer policy and once with a no-referrer control.
then: Expects the same-origin policy to send the page origin, and the no-referrer control to send a null Origin.
notes: Gated: the test skips unless STEGO_REQUIRE_BROWSER_LOGOUT is 1, and then it runs only in CI with Chrome or Chromium. It gives no proof on a developer workstation.

title: The emitted provider sign-out request is minimal
when: Builds the provider sign-out target for six unsafe discovered endpoints and for one valid HTTPS endpoint.
then: Expects a refusal for each unsafe endpoint, and expects exactly two query parameters, client_id and post_logout_redirect_uri, for the valid one.

title: The emitted provider sign-out refuses unsafe endpoints
when: Builds the provider sign-out target for six unsafe discovered endpoints and for one valid HTTPS endpoint.
then: Expects a refusal for each unsafe endpoint, and expects exactly two query parameters, client_id and post_logout_redirect_uri, for the valid one.

title: The emitted asset routes permit no broad script or style policy
when: Requests each declared route and asset, three undeclared paths, five unsafe return paths, and a plaintext or wrong-host address.
then: Expects a policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, the script hashes only on index.html, 404 for each undeclared path, / for each unsafe return path, and 400 for the wrong host.

title: The emitted script hashes apply only to the index document
when: Requests each declared route and asset, three undeclared paths, five unsafe return paths, and a plaintext or wrong-host address.
then: Expects a policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, the script hashes only on index.html, 404 for each undeclared path, / for each unsafe return path, and 400 for the wrong host.

title: The emitted backend refuses an identity host that shares the console cookie host
when: Starts the backend with an issuer on the console host and another port, then with a discovered authorization endpoint on the console host.
then: Expects the backend to refuse to start in both cases.

title: The emitted backend refuses an upstream on the console cookie host
when: Starts the backend with eight invalid upstream addresses, four of them on the console host.
then: Expects each start to fail.

title: The emitted key reader accepts only a small ring of distinct canonical keys
when: Reads four valid key files, then twenty-six invalid files with bad size, bad base64, a duplicate key, four keys, unknown or repeated JSON fields and trailing data.
then: Expects the valid files to keep their key order, and expects every invalid file to return the fixed error with a nil key ring.

title: The emitted backend checks its key file before database or provider access
when: Starts the backend with a key ring that repeats one key and with no database connection, among the other key switch steps.
then: Expects startup to fail with a key error.

title: The emitted store keeps old sessions readable across a key rollout
when: Reads one old record through four key rings, writes through two mixed writers, then signs out during a key switch.
then: Expects every listed key to decrypt, the first key to encrypt new records, a removed key to lose access, and a renewal after sign-out to fail.

title: A backend key switch keeps the browser session
when: Starts one backend with the old key first and one with the new key first, reads the session from each, then signs out on one.
then: Expects both backends to read the session, and the old writer not to restore it after sign-out.

title: The emitted backend reduces unsafe return paths to the root route
when: Requests each declared route and asset, three undeclared paths, five unsafe return paths, and a plaintext or wrong-host address.
then: Expects a policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, the script hashes only on index.html, 404 for each undeclared path, / for each unsafe return path, and 400 for the wrong host.

title: The completion document reduces an unsafe return target to the root route
when: Renders the completion document for nine return targets: local, a quoted query, absolute, a network path, an auth route, a fragment, an encoded path, a header injection and an over-long path.
then: Expects the safe targets to stay, and every unsafe target to become the root route.

title: The emitted backend returns 404 for undeclared paths
when: Requests each declared route and asset, three undeclared paths, five unsafe return paths, and a plaintext or wrong-host address.
then: Expects a policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, the script hashes only on index.html, 404 for each undeclared path, / for each unsafe return path, and 400 for the wrong host.

title: The local application proxy returns 404 for an undeclared UI route
when: Requests an undeclared UI route with a valid session, among the other denied requests.
then: Expects 404.

title: A storage failure reports temporary unavailability and keeps the cookie
when: Closes the database, then asks for the session.
then: Expects 503 with Retry-After 1 and no Set-Cookie header.

title: The emitted callback consumes a pending login exactly once
when: Sends a callback with a wrong state, then sends the same valid callback from two backend instances at the same time.
then: Expects no code exchange for the wrong state, one success and one denial for the concurrent pair, and exactly one exchange.

title: A rejected identity token gets no session and is revoked
when: Completes a callback for eight provider modes with a bad nonce, issuer, audience, expiry, issue time, auth time, roles or access token hash.
then: Expects 502 for each mode, no session cookie, and eight token revocations.

title: A rejected API session returns the fixed reauthentication response
when: Sends an API request with no session, then with a session the upstream rejects, then repeats it.
then: Expects the fixed 401 body, the WWW-Authenticate and no-store headers, no forwarded Location or ETag, a cleared cookie, and one upstream call.

title: The completion document holds no private state
when: Completes a protected application callback, then replays the same callback.
then: Expects a Strict, Secure, HttpOnly, host-only cookie, no session ID, token, code or state in the body, and 400 with no document for the replay.

title: The completion document holds no active markup and keeps its privacy headers
when: Renders the completion document for nine safe and unsafe return targets.
then: Expects one refresh and one link, no script, no cookie, no-store, no referrer, and a policy that permits no active or framed content.

title: Each index document gets a fresh style nonce
when: Requests the index document three times with dynamic styles enabled, then an asset, then an invalid insertion offset.
then: Expects three distinct 32-byte nonces that match their own document and policy, a changed ETag each time, no nonce on the asset, and a closed failure for the bad offset.

title: The runtime refuses a changed grant on its session table
when: Adds a schema CREATE grant, adds a grant option, and removes the DELETE grant.
then: Expects both Verify and Bootstrap to refuse each case.

title: The runtime login of the managed schema has only data access
when: Sets up the schema, then runs data statements and four schema statements as the runtime login.
then: Expects the data statements to succeed and each schema statement to be denied with code 42501.

title: The inserted runtime metadata is escaped and changes no policy
when: Requests the index document before and after the telemetry service name is set, with the earlier ETag.
then: Expects a fresh response, the escaped stego-runtime-config element, a disabled export for a missing collector, and the same content security policy.

title: The authorization request keeps the declared scopes
when: Starts login with one declared scope and then with four declared scopes.
then: Expects the authorization request's scope parameter to equal the declared value each time.

title: An API permission denial does not end a valid session
when: Makes the upstream API answer 403, then 401.
then: Expects the session to stay authenticated after the 403 and to end after the 401.

title: The pending login limit is enforced
when: Inserts 1,000 pending logins with one bounded statement, then creates one more.
then: Expects the store error and exactly 1,000 remaining records.

title: A cross-site request cannot read a private response
when: Sends the public page and three private routes with a cross-site and then a same-site fetch site, holding a valid cookie.
then: Expects 200 for the public page and 403 for the session, login and API routes.

title: The emitted JSON reader accepts only strict documents
when: Reads seven invalid documents with a repeated name, a lone surrogate, trailing data or deep nesting, then three valid documents.
then: Expects every invalid document refused and every valid document accepted.

title: The application upstream address stays compiler-owned
when: Starts the backend with a plaintext upstream, a foreign upstream and an unused trust file from the service environment.
then: Expects a compiler-owned error for each attempt.

title: The emitted backend refuses an upstream address that is not compiler-owned
when: Starts the backend with eight invalid upstream addresses: the console host, a plaintext address, a path and a query.
then: Expects each start to fail.

title: The proxy passes an upstream cache response through
when: Makes the upstream answer 304 and sends a conditional API request.
then: Expects 304, an empty body and the upstream ETag.

title: Telemetry ingest needs a session, an origin, a CSRF token and protobuf
when: Sends seven ingest requests with a missing session, missing CSRF token, missing Origin, wrong media type, wrong method, unknown path or oversize body, then a browser bearer token and compressed input.
then: Expects the stated status for each case and expects no telemetry at the API.

title: Telemetry admission bounds the burst and the session map
when: Takes six admissions for one session, then one more, then fills the session map and asks for another session.
then: Expects the six admissions, the refusal after them, and a 512-entry bound on the map.

title: Socket admission bounds each session and each backend
when: Takes two sockets for one session and then a third, ends the session, fills the backend capacity, then closes the set.
then: Expects the busy error for the third session socket, the cancellation on end, the busy error at backend capacity, and no socket after close.

title: A socket upgrade needs a session and an exact origin
when: Dials the socket route without a session, with a wrong Origin, with no Origin, with a browser bearer token, and with a denied query.

title: A socket survives the HTTP deadlines and relays both message kinds
when: Opens a socket through a server with 80 ms deadlines, waits 120 ms, then relays a binary and a text message and ends the session.
then: Expects both messages returned without a change, the exit status in the close reason, and a 101 upgrade status in the telemetry wrapper.

title: Every session end closes that session's sockets
when: Ends the session through local sign-out, remote sign-out, backend close, runtime stop, a storage failure, session expiry and token expiry.
then: Expects the socket to close in each mode and expects no socket lease to remain.
notes: Gated: the test needs a database and skips unless STEGO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN names one. It therefore gives no proof on a developer workstation, and proves its contracts only in a run that sets the variable. Lathe counts it as automated, which does not distinguish a test that runs from one that skips.

title: The socket data budget counts messages, bytes and empty frames
when: Offers data at the message bound, at the byte bound, an empty message at the last slot, and one oversize message.
then: Expects a refusal at each bound, the empty message counted, and the oversize message refused.

title: The local application proxy drops every untrusted browser header
when: Sends authenticated application requests, and a second backend's requests, with a cookie and four client-supplied identity headers.
then: Expects the server access token at the application, all five untrusted headers absent, and no private header in the response.

title: A local application write needs an exact origin and a trusted fetch site
when: Sends POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE with a missing, foreign or repeated Origin and with four fetch site values, then with a valid pair.
then: Expects 403 or 400 for every unsafe combination and 200 for the exact origin with a same-origin or absent fetch site.

title: The application CSRF check needs an exact origin and a trusted fetch site
when: Checks a write request with four untrusted fetch site values, with no Origin, then with the exact Origin.
then: Expects only the exact Origin with no untrusted fetch site to pass.

title: An anonymous document request starts login and keeps the cookie
when: Requests an API path and an asset with no session, a declared route by direct navigation, then the landing page cross-site.
then: Expects 401 for the private paths, a 303 to the login route for the document, the sign-in page cross-site, and no Set-Cookie header.

title: A captured asset needs a session and stops after sign-out
when: Reads each captured path from two backends with a session, anonymously, conditionally, with a browser bearer token, then after sign-out.
then: Expects no-store and no token in every body, 401 for an anonymous read, 400 for the bearer token, and 401 on the second backend after sign-out.

title: Schema setup is locked and repeatable
when: Runs two owner connections through Bootstrap at the same time, repeats the setup, then runs data and schema statements as the runtime login.
then: Expects both owners to succeed, an unchanged catalog snapshot after the repeat, the four data statements to pass, and four schema statements to be denied.

title: A failed schema setup rolls back
when: Adds an unsafe default table grant and runs Bootstrap, then removes the grant and runs Bootstrap again.
then: Expects the first setup to fail and leave no table, and the second setup to succeed.

title: Startup refuses a schema that differs from the generated one
when: Changes the table, a column, a constraint or an index, then verifies the schema.
then: Expects the runtime to refuse startup for each change.

title: Schema setup refuses invalid input
when: Calls Verify and Bootstrap with a nil context, a nil connection and an unsafe role name.
then: Expects the fixed schema error for each call.

title: Startup diagnostics name each stage and hold no private input
when: Runs the generated runtime in a child process for six failure points and one success, with private markers in every configuration value.
then: Expects one completion record per stage in order, the correct outcome for the last stage, only the ten permitted fields, and no private marker in the output.

title: A startup step keeps its error, its context and its panic
when: Runs a startup step for a nil error, a cancellation, a deadline and a private error, then one that panics.
then: Expects the same error value, exactly one call, the caller's own context, and the panic passed through unchanged.

title: A failed renewal claim leaves the session usable
when: Injects a lost row, a cancellation and a deadline at the claim read, then renews the session again.
then: Expects the store error, an active session with its original credentials, no refresh token use, and one successful later renewal.

title: A cancelled renewal leaves no refresh claim
when: Pauses the provider inside the renewal, then cancels the caller.
then: Expects the renewal to fail and expects no retained refresh claim in the store.

title: The emitted runtime uses the fixed same-origin transport

then: Expects one POST to each of the three same-origin signal paths, same-origin credentials with a refused redirect, the session token in the header only, the generated service name in every body, and no reported failure.

title: The emitted runtime sends each batch with a session token

title: An unauthenticated session makes no export request

then: Expects the flush to fail, no export request, and no reporter error outside the runtime.

title: The emitted runtime uses the generated service identity

title: Export failures stay inside the public categories

title: Processor queue loss is reported for logs and traces

then: Expects the reporter to receive queue_full for traces and for logs.

title: Export failures stay inside the response limit
when: Answers an export with a private error body, then with a partial-success record, then with a response above 16 KiB.

title: A stalled export reaches its deadline and a terminal result

title: The emitted runtime refuses an insecure page
when: Supplies invalid options and invalid root trace IDs, then moves the page to http.
then: Expects every invalid option and trace ID refused, a valid span ID shape, no fetch call, and a refusal to start on the http page.

title: The emitted runtime refuses an invalid trace ID
when: Supplies invalid options and invalid root trace IDs, then moves the page to http.
then: Expects every invalid option and trace ID refused, a valid span ID shape, no fetch call, and a refusal to start on the http page.

title: An invalid entropy source cannot give a zero trace ID
when: Replaces the random source with one that gives only zeros, then generates a trace ID.
then: Expects an entropy error after exactly three attempts.

title: The emitted runtime holds its log, instrument and attribute limits
when: Emits a log body of 513 characters and an object log body, creates 33 counters, then adds a value with a 257-character attribute.
then: Expects no log export, two invalid_record reports for logs and two for metrics, so the limits refuse the records before export.

title: Observable metric callbacks use the direct write limits and release their capacity
when: Registers the same callback twice on an observable gauge, counter and up-down counter, observes one valid value, an oversized attribute, an array attribute and an infinite value, then removes each registration.
then: Expects three collections for three instruments, nine invalid_record reports, the valid series exported, the oversized and array attributes absent from the payload, and no further collection after removal.

title: Batch observable callbacks use the direct write limits and release their capacity
when: Registers one batch callback twice for a gauge and a counter, observes valid values, an oversized attribute and NaN, then removes the registration.
then: Expects one callback run, two invalid records, only valid values in the export, and no run after removal.

title: Observable callbacks share a registration limit and a bounded collection

title: Batch observable callbacks observe only their selected instruments
when: Registers one batch callback twice for a gauge and a counter with repeated selections, then observes both instruments.
then: Expects one callback run, and values only for the selected instruments.

title: Public deployment metadata controls each exporter
when: Supplies no metadata element, then an all-off element, then an element with traces and metrics on, then an out-of-range ratio, then an element with an extra key.
then: Expects exports only for the single valid element and only for its enabled signals, and no export for absent or invalid metadata.

title: Server rendering creates no browser transport
when: Removes the page location, then records a span, a log and a metric and runs flush and shutdown.
then: Expects no fetch call at all, so the server render creates no exporter, provider or timer.

title: A hidden page flushes and shutdown happens once
when: Records one span, raises a page-hide event, calls shutdown twice, then raises the event again.
then: Expects the trace export after the first event, the same result object for both shutdown calls, and no further call after shutdown, so the listeners are removed.

title: The emitted runtime puts no credential in an export body
when: Starts the emitted runtime on an HTTPS page, records one span, one log and one metric, then flushes.
then: Expects one POST to each of the three same-origin signal paths, same-origin credentials with a refused redirect, the session token in the header only, the generated service name in every body, and no reported failure.

title: The emitted package and its declarations compile and run under strict checks
when: Writes the emitted files to a temporary project with the pinned dependencies, then runs the Node runtime fixture and compiles testdata/usage.mts with strict TypeScript, bounded target and NodeNext resolution.

title: The emitted CLI accepts only verified HTTPS
when: Logs in with a token file against a TLS server, runs create, read, list and delete commands, rotates the token, then supplies a public configuration, a writable configuration directory, a public token file, a configuration symlink, a FIFO, invalid arguments, invalid body files, a redirect answer, a private error answer and a duplicate-key answer, and finally an http destination.
then: Expects mode 0600 configuration without the token, the rotated token read by the next command, exact response numbers, each unsafe or invalid case refused, one request for each rejected answer, no private text or token in an error, and the external token file retained after logout.

title: The emitted CLI reserves a private output file before the request
when: Runs a sensitive scoped command with no output option, then with an existing file, a symlink, a FIFO, a directory, a writable parent and a missing parent, then with a new file, a repeated file, a failed API answer and an explicit stdout selection.
then: Expects the empty private reservation present during the request, every unsafe destination refused with no stdout output, the secret written only to the new private file, an existing file never replaced, the empty reservation removed after a failure, and only the name field in the request body.

when: Writes output through a writer that fails, a writer that writes short, and a closed file.

then: Expects each invalid input to fail before any request, and the wrong write answer to give the status unknown with no retry.

title: The output file is reserved before a token refresh
when: Saves an expired OIDC session, then runs a command with an existing output file.
then: Expects the command to fail with no token request and the file unchanged.

title: A sensitive command of the emitted CLI needs an output file
when: Runs a sensitive scoped command with no output option, then with an existing file, a symlink, a FIFO, a directory, a writable parent and a missing parent, then with a new file, a repeated file, a failed API answer and an explicit stdout selection.

title: The emitted CLI reports only API identity
when: Runs the identity command against a TLS API, then requests raw and decoded token output with and without an output file, with both options together, and against a failed, incomplete and duplicate-key answer.
then: Expects the report built from the API answer only, the token and the private and local claims absent from the default output, token export refused without an output file and without an API call, mode 0600 export files with exact decoded numbers, and no output file after a failure.

title: The emitted CLI exports a token only to a private file
when: Runs the identity command against a TLS API, then requests raw and decoded token output with and without an output file, with both options together, and against a failed, incomplete and duplicate-key answer.
then: Expects the report built from the API answer only, the token and the private and local claims absent from the default output, token export refused without an output file and without an API call, mode 0600 export files with exact decoded numbers, and no output file after a failure.

title: The emitted CLI holds the restricted OIDC profile at browser login
when: Runs browser login against a TLS provider that returns a wrong issuer, a plaintext token endpoint, a wrong nonce, a wrong audience, an expired token, a wrong authorized party, a wrong token hash and a changed issuer claim, and answers the callback with a wrong state and then twice with the correct state.

then: Expects login after two polls with no private value in the display, and a delayed next poll after slow_down.

then: Expects no credential from the failed refresh, exactly one provider refresh across both attempts, a refusal of the second attempt, and the pending record still in the saved session.

then: Expects the request to fail with no token request.

title: The rendered service and worker Pods mount no service-account token

then: The service Pod and the worker Pod mount no service-account token.

title: The browser Pod mounts no token and uses no host namespace
