then: The Pod mounts no token and uses no host namespace.

title: The rendered service probes use HTTPS
when: The generator writes a project with a worker and an RPC process, and the generated renderer runs for each workload with valid and invalid arguments.
then: The startup, liveness and readiness probes of the service container use HTTPS.

title: The rendered external egress rules stay narrow
when: The generator writes a project with a worker and an RPC process, and the generated renderer runs for each workload with valid and invalid arguments.
then: Each external endpoint rule holds one host prefix and one TCP port.

title: An incomplete or wrong endpoint binding gives no rendered manifest
when: The generator writes a project with a worker and an RPC process, and the generated renderer runs for each workload with valid and invalid arguments.
then: A missing, undeclared, repeated or cross-scope endpoint binding, or an unknown workload, returns an error and no output.

title: A browser deployment refuses a gRPC ingress peer
when: The generator runs once for a rest-api declaration and once for the equivalent browser-backend declaration, and then the browser declaration adds an ingress peer on port 9090.
then: The declaration with the 9090 ingress peer is refused.

title: The rendered worker has no Service, container port or ingress rule
when: The generator writes a project with a worker and an RPC process, and the generated renderer runs for each workload with valid and invalid arguments.
then: The worker manifest has no Service, its container has no port, and its NetworkPolicy has no ingress rule.

title: The rendered worker uses Recreate and sets no replica count
when: The generator writes a project with a worker and an RPC process, and the generated renderer runs for each workload with valid and invalid arguments.
then: The worker Deployment uses the Recreate strategy and carries no replicas field.
notes: The code still emits replicas: 1 (internal/generator/kubernetesservice/workers.go), so this test proves the old contract until the generator and the test change together; see ST-DLV-INV08.

title: The rendered RPC Service exposes only port 9090
when: The generator writes a project with a worker and an RPC process, and the generated renderer runs for each workload with valid and invalid arguments.
then: The RPC Service exposes exactly one port, 9090.

title: The RPC Deployment sets no replica count and keeps the selected rollout strategy
when: The test renders the RPC manifest for the default declaration, then for an explicit RollingUpdate choice and an explicit Recreate choice.
then: No Deployment carries a replicas field. The default and the explicit RollingUpdate strategy use one extra Pod and zero unavailable Pods. Recreate carries no rolling-update settings. The file set, the file paths and every other resource stay equal to the default output.
notes: The code still emits replicas: 1 (internal/generator/kubernetesservice/rpc.go), so this test proves the old contract until the generator and the test change together; see ST-DLV-INV08.

title: An invalid image, namespace or file group gives no rendered output
when: The generator writes a project with a worker and an RPC process, and the generated renderer runs for each workload with valid and invalid arguments.
then: An image without a registry and a digest, a namespace that is not a DNS label, and a zero file group each return an error and no output.

title: The generated renderer splits scopes and keeps every object
when: The generator writes a project with allocation, RPC and Kubernetes access, and the generated scope, library and configuration checks run against the renderer.
then: The cluster and namespace manifests together hold the same objects as the full manifest, each with its own scope. An unknown kind or a wrong namespace stops the render.

title: The generated renderer sets the configuration digest in one annotation
when: The generator writes a project with allocation, RPC and Kubernetes access, and the generated scope, library and configuration checks run against the renderer.
then: A supplied digest changes only the Pod template annotation, and an invalid digest returns no output.

title: The generated renderer keeps generated labels against owner labels
when: The generator writes a project with allocation, RPC and Kubernetes access, and the generated scope, library and configuration checks run against the renderer.
then: An owner label that conflicts with a generated label is refused.

title: The generated renderer adds pull Secrets as name references
when: The generator writes a project with allocation, RPC and Kubernetes access, and the generated scope, library and configuration checks run against the renderer.
then: Pull Secrets appear as name references.

title: The Pod admission policy fails closed and its binding denies
when: A profile adds a Pod runtime class and a declared Pod ServiceAccount, and the test compares the generated objects with the earlier set.
then: The new policy fails closed, its binding denies, and it selects only the installation marker and the profile.

title: Every isolated allocation policy fails closed
when: An isolated profile declares an account, network isolation, a runtime class, Pod annotations and a capability grant, and the test reads every generated object.
then: All eight policies fail closed.

title: The isolated allocator gets no policy or runtime class write
when: An isolated profile declares an account, network isolation, a runtime class, Pod annotations and a capability grant, and the test reads every generated object.
then: No generated ClusterRole names validatingadmissionpolicies or runtimeclasses.

title: Network isolation gives narrow NetworkPolicy permissions
when: One profile selects network isolation and a second profile does not, and the test reads the generated roles and policies.
then: The allocator receives get and patch on the name stego-allocation plus create and list, and no update or delete. A profile without isolation receives no network permission.

title: Network isolation gives a deny-all policy shape
when: One profile selects network isolation and a second profile does not, and the test reads the generated roles and policies.
then: The admission guard requires the reserved name, an empty Pod selector, both policy types and no allow rule. It selects only the isolated profile.

title: The control account installer role carries one capability and no binding
when: The test reads every generated object for a plain declaration and for a declaration with related profiles.
then: The control account guard selects the control namespace on create and fails closed. Its expression reserves the fixed control account names and the generateName prefixes, and requires the installer capability. The installer ClusterRole holds one non-resource rule with the verb get. No ClusterRoleBinding selects that role, and no other generated object carries the capability.

title: The Pod admission policy covers status and ephemeral container writes
when: A profile adds a Pod runtime class and a declared Pod ServiceAccount, and the test compares the generated objects with the earlier set.
then: Its rules cover pods, pods/status and pods/ephemeralcontainers on CREATE and UPDATE.

title: The Pod admission policy holds the account and token rules
when: A profile adds a Pod runtime class and a declared Pod ServiceAccount, and the test compares the generated objects with the earlier set.
then: Its validations name the sealed account annotation, the automatic token field, the runtime class and the owner label.

title: A profile without a runtime class emits no runtime-class admission rule
when: An isolated profile declares an account and network isolation but no Pod runtime class, and the test reads every generated object.
then: The profile keeps the isolated security mode with an empty runtime class. No generated policy names runtimeClassName. The number of generated policies does not change.

title: An application Pod rule adds one denial and changes nothing else
when: An isolated profile adds one CEL Pod rule, and the test compares the generated policy with the policy built without that rule.
then: The rule is the last validation and keeps its exact expression and message. After the test removes it, the policy and the binding are equal to the earlier objects. The allocator runtime configuration holds no expression code. A repeated rule is refused.

title: Only the assigned network node identity can change the Pod network output annotation
when: The test compiles the generated rule for the OVN key and for the Multus key, then evaluates it for each request case.
then: The rule permits the assigned node to add, change or remove its own output through a status update, and permits a create request and an ordinary update that preserve the value. It denies a workload write, another node, a spoofed username prefix, a wrong or missing group, another subresource, a main-resource write, a create injection, a changed node assignment and a missing assignment.

title: The browser Pod keeps the local application container inside a separate boundary
when: A browser service declares one local application, and the test renders the generated manifest template.
then: The application container has no port, its own Secret and temporary volumes, no volume shared with the browser, and a fixed loopback listener. The Service exposes only port 8443, and a peer for the application port is refused.

title: A browser deployment matches the API deployment byte for byte
when: The generator runs once for a rest-api declaration and once for the equivalent browser-backend declaration, and then the browser declaration adds an ingress peer on port 9090.
then: Both file sets have the same length, and each file has the same path and the same bytes. The declaration with the 9090 ingress peer is refused.

title: The RPC image and manifest carry the declared process, its TLS listener and its loopback monitor
when: The generator writes the files for one declared RPC process twice.
then: Both passes write the same bytes. The RPC Containerfile builds the declared process path and declares the explicit entry point. The RPC manifest names its own service account, both probe modes, the loopback monitor address, the gRPC listen address and the TLS key path.

title: The generated renderer refuses an invalid existing account or scope
when: Renders with existing account names that hold a path, a dot, an upper-case letter, a lone hyphen or 64 characters, and with a valid name under the empty, all and cluster scopes.
then: Expects an error and no output for each.
notes: Proved by TestExistingServiceAccountRejectsAmbiguousAuthority; its name or a subtest must carry this ID. The spec recorded this feature as under qualification.

title: The generated renderer checks the whole list before it filters
when: Applies the existing account to generated lists that lack the account or the Deployment, repeat one of them, name another namespace or account, lack the Pod, hold an unknown kind, or hold a ClusterRoleBinding.
then: Expects an error and no output for each.
notes: Proved by TestExistingServiceAccountRejectsInvalidGeneratedIdentity; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The generated renderer changes only the Pod account reference
when: Renders an RPC workload with owner labels and a pull Secret, then again with an existing account, twice, and once from the command line.
then: Expects no ServiceAccount, the selected name in the Pod, every other resource equal, byte-equal repeat output, and the command output equal to the typed output.
notes: Proved by TestExistingServiceAccountPreservesWorkload; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The built Pod and container keep the restricted security context
when: The generated library builds one Deployment and one Service from a complete widget declaration.
then: The Pod uses the expected non-root security context with the RuntimeDefault profile. Each container uses the expected restricted security context.

title: The built resources hold no host, privileged, subPath or exec field
when: The generated library builds one Deployment and one Service from a complete widget declaration.
then: The serialized output holds no host, privileged, subPath or exec field.

title: The built Pod mounts no service-account token
when: The generated library builds one Deployment and one Service from a complete widget declaration.
then: The Pod does not mount the service-account token and uses the declared service account.

title: An unsafe service account returns no resources
when: Each case sets the default service account or an empty service account, and calls Build.
then: Build returns the fixed declaration error and no resources.

title: The built Secret and ConfigMap mounts are read-only
when: The generated library builds one Deployment and one Service from a complete widget declaration.
then: The Secret volume uses mode 0440. The Secret and ConfigMap mounts are read-only, and the temporary mount is writable.

title: An unbounded or ambiguous volume returns no resources
when: Each case sets a volume with two sources, a negative emptyDir size or an emptyDir size above the storage limit, and calls Build.
then: Build returns the fixed declaration error and no resources.

title: The built container keeps three HTTP probes with deadlines and no host
when: The generated library builds one Deployment and one Service from a complete widget declaration.
then: The startup, readiness and liveness probes keep their deadlines and have no host.

title: An unsafe or incomplete probe returns no resources
when: Each case sets a probe with a wrong port, a host, a query, an encoded path, a new line, or a zero timeout, period or threshold, and calls Build.
then: Build returns the fixed declaration error and no resources.

title: An image without a registry or digest returns no resources
when: Each case sets an image with a tag and no digest, a malformed digest, a scheme, or an invalid registry host or port, and calls Build.
then: Build returns the fixed declaration error and no resources.

title: Changed dependency contents change only the configuration annotation
when: The declaration keeps every other field and rotates one Secret value, then changes one ConfigMap value.
then: The Pod template annotation stego.dev/config-sha256 changes each time. The rest of the Pod template is equal to the earlier template.

title: The built resources hold no dependency contents
when: The generated library builds one Deployment and one Service from a complete widget declaration.
then: The serialized output holds no dependency value.

title: A rotated Secret value does not appear in the output
when: The declaration keeps every other field and rotates one Secret value.
then: The serialized output holds no rotated Secret value.

title: A dependency that does not match the mounts and environment returns no resources
when: Each case sets a missing, extra or wrong-kind dependency, a missing environment key, a mount of an unknown volume or an unused volume, and calls Build.
then: Build returns the fixed declaration error and no resources.

title: The built Service is a ClusterIP Service that targets the declared port
when: The generated library builds one Deployment and one Service from a complete widget declaration.
then: The Service is a ClusterIP Service that targets the declared container port.

title: An omitted profile field stays an explicit null and survives the API response format
when: The declaration omits the container arguments, the environment, the mounts, the volumes and the dependencies, and the test then adds one empty environment value and reads the full widget mounts.
then: The Pod holds a present null for its volume and pull-Secret fields. The container holds a present null for its argument, environment and mount fields. An empty environment value and a false mount flag still match after the upstream omit rules serialize them.

title: A zero or excess resource amount returns no resources
when: Each case sets a zero or excess resource request or a negative limit, and calls Build.
then: Build returns the fixed declaration error and no resources.

title: A span from the emitted runtime holds no private request data
when: Sends one request that holds a private path, query, body, Authorization header, baggage and trace state through the emitted handler, with dead HTTP proxy variables set, and reads the exported trace.
then: Expects the application status and body unchanged, a valid span context in the handler, one span with two attributes and no trace state, and no private value in the serialized export.

title: The emitted handler wrapper keeps the application status and body
when: Sends one request that holds a private path, query, body, Authorization header, baggage and trace state through the emitted handler, with dead HTTP proxy variables set, and reads the exported trace.
then: Expects the application status and body unchanged, a valid span context in the handler, one span with two attributes and no trace state, and no private value in the serialized export.

title: The emitted runtime refuses a collector endpoint that is not a plain HTTPS origin
when: Builds the runtime with no collector, then with a plaintext, credentialed, path-bearing and query-bearing endpoint, then with five invalid sampling ratios, then with an undeclared resource attribute setting.
then: Expects no provider without a collector, and a refusal for every invalid endpoint, every invalid ratio and the undeclared setting.

title: The emitted runtime refuses an undeclared OTEL setting
when: Builds the runtime with no collector, then with a plaintext, credentialed, path-bearing and query-bearing endpoint, then with five invalid sampling ratios, then with an undeclared resource attribute setting.
then: Expects no provider without a collector, and a refusal for every invalid endpoint, every invalid ratio and the undeclared setting.

title: The emitted runtime refuses a sampling ratio outside 0 to 1
when: Builds the runtime with no collector, then with a plaintext, credentialed, path-bearing and query-bearing endpoint, then with five invalid sampling ratios, then with an undeclared resource attribute setting.
then: Expects no provider without a collector, and a refusal for every invalid endpoint, every invalid ratio and the undeclared setting.

title: The emitted runtime does not export to an untrusted collector
when: Removes the collector certificate setting, then observes one request and waits for an export failure.
then: Expects the export failure count to rise and the collector to receive no trace.

title: The emitted runtime exports past dead HTTP proxy settings
when: Sends one request that holds a private path, query, body, Authorization header, baggage and trace state through the emitted handler, with dead HTTP proxy variables set, and reads the exported trace.
then: Expects the application status and body unchanged, a valid span context in the handler, one span with two attributes and no trace state, and no private value in the serialized export.

title: A blocked collector does not change or delay a request the emitted runtime observes
when: Observes three times the queue size in requests against a collector that never answers, then closes the runtime.
then: Expects every request to keep its status, the whole request set to finish inside one second, an export failure to be recorded, and shutdown to finish inside its limit.

title: The emitted runtime finishes shutdown inside its limit when the collector is blocked
when: Observes three times the queue size in requests against a collector that never answers, then closes the runtime.
then: Expects every request to keep its status, the whole request set to finish inside one second, an export failure to be recorded, and shutdown to finish inside its limit.

title: The emitted runtime attaches the collector token to every signal
when: Exports traces, logs and metrics to a TLS collector that requires one bearer token, replaces the token file, exports again, then makes the token file world readable.
then: Expects every signal accepted with the first token, every signal accepted with the replacement token without a restart, and a refused export after the file permission change.

title: The emitted runtime applies a replaced collector token without a restart
when: Exports traces, logs and metrics to a TLS collector that requires one bearer token, replaces the token file, exports again, then makes the token file world readable.
then: Expects every signal accepted with the first token, every signal accepted with the replacement token without a restart, and a refused export after the file permission change.

title: The emitted runtime refuses a collector token file that others can read
when: Exports traces, logs and metrics to a TLS collector that requires one bearer token, replaces the token file, exports again, then makes the token file world readable.
then: Expects every signal accepted with the first token, every signal accepted with the replacement token without a restart, and a refused export after the file permission change.

title: The emitted runtime identity is a UUID v4 from the random source
when: Builds an instance ID from a fixed 17-byte reader, then from a short reader and from a reader that returns an error.
then: Expects the canonical UUID v4 encoding from exactly 16 bytes, and an empty value with fixed error text that holds no private detail for each failing reader.

title: The emitted runtime fails with fixed text on an entropy failure
when: Builds an instance ID from a fixed 17-byte reader, then from a short reader and from a reader that returns an error.
then: Expects the canonical UUID v4 encoding from exactly 16 bytes, and an empty value with fixed error text that holds no private detail for each failing reader.

title: A remote sampled flag cannot override the local zero ratio of the emitted runtime
when: Sets the sampling ratio to zero and sends a request that carries a sampled trace parent.
then: Expects the handler span not recording and no trace exported.

title: An invalid trace parent starts a root span in the emitted runtime
when: Sends four requests whose trace parent is absent, malformed, all zero and repeated.
then: Expects one exported root span for each request.

title: The emitted metric provider limits each instrument to 128 series
when: Starts one stream, then records three cycles of twice the series limit of distinct RPC methods, and flushes the meter after each cycle.
then: Expects the active counter at one for the open stream, no more than the series limit of histogram series, an overflow series that keeps every count, and the active counter back at zero.

title: The emitted active request counter returns to zero
when: Starts one stream, then records three cycles of twice the series limit of distinct RPC methods, and flushes the meter after each cycle.
then: Expects the active counter at one for the open stream, no more than the series limit of histogram series, an overflow series that keeps every count, and the active counter back at zero.

title: Concurrent and replacement emitted runtimes hold distinct identities
when: Creates and closes thirty-two runtimes at the same time with one service name.
then: Expects thirty-two valid and distinct UUID identities, and no change to an identity across its close.

title: Every signal and the local log of the emitted runtime share its identity
when: Observes one request, logs one service event, closes the runtime, and reads the local output with the exported traces, logs and metrics.
then: Expects the same service name and instance identity in the local record and in all three exported signals, with two resource attributes only.

title: A handler panic in the emitted runtime invents no response and is raised again
when: Sends one request to a handler that panics with a private value, then reads the exported metrics and logs.
then: Expects the panic re-raised, no status attribute on the duration metric, error.type panic, the active counter at zero, an ERROR log record, and no private value in the export.

title: A handler panic leaves no active request in the emitted runtime
when: Sends one request to a handler that panics with a private value, then reads the exported metrics and logs.
then: Expects the panic re-raised, no status attribute on the duration metric, error.type panic, the active counter at zero, an ERROR log record, and no private value in the export.

title: A blocked local log output of the emitted runtime stays bounded and does not block its caller
when: Holds the local writer inside one record, then logs three times the queue size of events, then closes the runtime.
then: Expects the caller never blocked, the drop count equal to the records beyond the bound, the shared shutdown budget held, and a refusal after the queue closes.

title: Outbound RPC signals from the emitted runtime keep the parent trace and isolate the caller metadata
when: Traces three outbound calls inside a caller span, with private authorization, trace parent, trace state and baggage metadata, for a sampled and an unsampled ratio.
then: Expects a child span of the caller trace, one injected trace parent with no trace state or baggage, the caller metadata unchanged, one completion for each call, the active counter at zero, and no private value in the export.

title: Database signals from the emitted runtime hold no statement data and map an unknown outcome
when: Traces six database calls with a private call name and the six outcome values, including a private outcome, for a sampled and an unsampled ratio.
then: Expects one completion for each call, the private outcome recorded as the fixed failure value, correlated client spans, idempotent completion, and no private value in the export.

title: The emitted deployment export returns fixed file names and no private value
when: Exports a deployment environment from validated settings, replaces the token file and exports again, then exports for nine invalid cases.
then: Expects the fixed relative file names with the captured file contents, no token or source path in the environment, the replacement token in the later call with the earlier capture unchanged, every invalid case refused, and no private value in the error.

title: Outbound HTTPS signals from the emitted runtime keep the parent trace and send no private propagation
when: Traces five outbound HTTPS calls inside a caller span, with private authorization, trace parent, trace state and baggage headers, for a sampled and an unsampled ratio.
then: Expects a child span of the caller trace, one trace parent header with no trace state or baggage, the caller headers unchanged, one completion for each call, and no private value in the export.

title: The emitted runtime refuses an unsupported exporter or metric interval
when: Builds the runtime for nine invalid exporter and interval values, then records three times the queue size of calls against a collector that never answers, then closes the runtime, then disables both signals.
then: Expects every invalid setting refused, the calls not delayed, the export failures counted, shutdown inside one shared limit, and no provider for a disabled signal.

title: Blocked signal collectors share one shutdown limit in the emitted runtime
when: Builds the runtime for nine invalid exporter and interval values, then records three times the queue size of calls against a collector that never answers, then closes the runtime, then disables both signals.
then: Expects every invalid setting refused, the calls not delayed, the export failures counted, shutdown inside one shared limit, and no provider for a disabled signal.

title: The emitted runtime refuses an invalid service name and does not echo it
when: Builds the runtime with a service name that holds a newline, with a 129-byte name and with a name that holds an equals sign.
then: Expects every name refused and the value absent from the error text.

title: The emitted queue commits the message with the application write
when: Writes an application row and enqueues one message in one transaction, then rolls back, and then repeats the same work and commits.
then: Expects no visible data before the end of the transaction, no row and no message after the rollback, and both after the commit.

title: The emitted queue refuses an invalid payload before it uses the database
when: Validates ten invalid payloads, one valid payload, an enqueue with no transaction and a queue with no database.
then: Expects every invalid payload refused, the valid payload accepted, and an error for the missing transaction and the missing database.

title: A retry holds only its own key
when: Claims two messages for one resource key and one for another key, retries the oldest message, and claims again.
then: Expects no claim for the successor during the delay, the same ID and a second attempt after it, and progress for the other key.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC18-OC04-T01.

title: A retry keeps the message identity
when: Claims two messages for one resource key and one for another key, retries the oldest message, and claims again.
then: Expects no claim for the successor during the delay, the same ID and a second attempt after it, and progress for the other key.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC18-OC03-T01.

title: A worker retry keeps the message identity
when: Fails the first delivery of one message with an error that holds a private value, then lets both messages succeed.
then: Expects three handler calls in order, the same ID for both attempts, one retry, no lost lease, and an empty queue.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC18-OC06-T02.

title: An expired lease cannot acknowledge or retry a message
when: Claims one message with a short lease, waits for the lease to expire, then acknowledges and retries with the old receipt.
then: Expects both calls to report no effect and the message to stay in the queue.

title: A changed lease token cannot acknowledge a message
when: Replaces the lease token in the database while the handler runs.
then: Expects one lost lease, no delivery, and the retained message.

title: The emitted worker stores no handler error text
when: Runs the worker with a handler that returns an error which holds a private value.
then: Expects the stored failure code 'delivery-failed' and no part of the handler's error text.

title: A worker retry stores no error text
when: Fails the first delivery of one message with an error that holds a private value, then lets both messages succeed.
then: Expects three handler calls in order, the same ID for both attempts, one retry, no lost lease, and an empty queue.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC18-OC04-T02.

title: A result after the attempt deadline is not acknowledged
when: Runs the worker with a handler that waits for its context to end and then returns success.
then: Expects no delivery count, a retry, and the stored failure code 'delivery-timeout'.

title: An attempt deadline retains the failed message
when: Runs a handler that waits for its context to end.
then: Expects the attempt to stop at its deadline and the message to stay in the queue for retry.

title: A claim with a lost client result returns no delivery
when: Runs the claim through a bounded SQL driver that returns a query error, and then a row error after one row.
then: Expects no delivery in both cases and the underlying error for the caller.

title: Recovery after an unknown claim result keeps the delivery contract
when: Loses the claim result, waits for normal lease expiry, and claims the message again.
then: Expects the same message IDs and contents, a higher attempt count, a new receipt token, and no effect from the old token.

title: A lost notice session stops the source and its subscriptions
when: Terminates the dedicated PostgreSQL backend of the source, then reads the subscription, subscribes again, and starts a replacement source.
then: Expects the supervised task and the subscription to fail with ErrEventSourceUnavailable, the failed source to refuse a new subscription, and the replacement source to deliver the next notice.

title: A repeated message ID stops the application write
when: Enqueues one message, then writes an application row and enqueues the same message ID in one transaction.
then: Expects the enqueue to fail, the commit to fail, no application row, and one stored message.

title: Notices reach every session after the commit, in commit order
when: Subscribes two separate sessions, enqueues inside an open transaction, commits, and then enqueues two messages for one resource key in one transaction.
then: Expects no notice before the commit, the notice in both sessions after it, and the two notices in commit order.

title: Concurrent enqueues serialize before the sequence
when: Enqueues for one resource key in one open transaction, then enqueues the same key in a second transaction, and commits the first.
then: Expects the second enqueue to wait for the predecessor, and expects the first message in the next claim.

title: Concurrent workers claim distinct messages
when: Runs eight workers that each claim eight of 32 queued messages.
then: Expects no error, 32 claimed messages, and no message in two batches.

title: An unknown destination stays in the queue
when: Enqueues a message for a destination that the worker has no handler for.
then: Expects the stored code 'destination-unknown', no handler call, and the unknown-destination counter above zero.

title: Unsafe worker limits are refused and the retry delay stays bounded
when: Builds the worker with seven unsafe configurations and with a nil handler, then samples the retry delay for four attempt counts.
then: Expects an error for each unsafe input, and every delay inside the configured bounds.

title: The worker holds its concurrency limit and copies its handlers
when: Queues eight messages, removes the handler from the caller's map after construction, and starts a second run.
then: Expects at most two active handlers, all eight deliveries, no active handler at the end, and an error from the second run.

title: A database failure drops no message
when: Closes the connection pool while the worker runs.
then: Expects the database-failure counter above zero and no delivery.

title: The blocked view holds one entry for each stuck key
when: Claims two of four messages, reads the blocked view, retries one key with a failure code, makes that key ready, and reads the view again with two invalid limits.
then: Expects one entry for each in-flight key with its destination and timing, the failure code retained, the ready key absent, and both invalid limits refused.

title: Dead letters and purge keep the unexhausted messages
when: Exhausts one resource key with three claims and retries, lists the dead letters, purges them, and gives an invalid limit.
then: Expects only the exhausted messages listed and removed, the fresh message retained, and the invalid limit refused.

title: A process crash commits nothing and releases its lease
when: Runs a helper subprocess that exits abruptly with an open transaction, and again with an active claim.
